title: Dead-letter queue persistence, retry, discard, and alert behavior fails
notes: Cluster E from the final integration run: TC-OBS-05-INT-01/02/03 and TC-OBS-06-INT-05 fail on dead-letter persistence/query/retry/discard and alert-state checks. Evidence: _integration_final.log lines 23075-23257.
root_cause: Three separate layers: (1) TC-OBS-05-INT-02/03 test SQL cast: audit_entries.resource_id is TEXT (migrated by GBL-120/ISS-103) but test queries used resource_id = $1::uuid causing C42804 TEXT=UUID mismatch; (2) Migration gap: GBL-121 fixed bpm_audit_resource_info to handle dead_letter_items in PUBLIC schema, but GBL-* migrations are skipped for tenant schemas by Migrations.runForSchema(); tenant_default.bpm_audit_resource_info retained the migration-020 version which only handled dead_letter_queue — after rename to dead_letter_items, r_id returned NULL, triggering a skip in bpm_audit_on_mutation, so no audit entries were created; (3) TC-OBS-05-INT-03 SAVEPOINT: the test used SAVEPOINT outside a transaction block and tried to create a trigger inside an uncommitted transaction, which is not visible to handleDiscard's separate pool connection. TC-SCH-303 was already passing. TC-OBS-06 was already passing.
candidate_resolution: Reconcile repository SQL and alert derivation with the canonical DLQ schema, define explicit retry/discard transitions, and verify persistence plus alert state transactionally against real PostgreSQL.
resolution: Fixed in WF03-GH379-20260809: (1) Changed resource_id = $1::uuid → resource_id = $1 in obs05_dlq_test.zig lines 395 and 462; (2) Added migration 1139_iss0116_dlq_audit_resource_info.sql which recreates bpm_audit_resource_info in tenant schemas (skipped by GBL-* guard) to handle dead_letter_items with resource_type='dlq'; (3) Replaced SAVEPOINT-based trigger isolation with defer-based cleanup and autocommit creation so the trigger is visible to handleDiscard's pool connection.
prevention: GBL-* migrations are skipped for tenant schemas — any migration that updates shared functions (audit triggers, resource info handlers) must be a numbered migration, not GBL-*, to run per-schema.
When renaming a table (dead_letter_queue → dead_letter_items), update all audit function handlers to include the new name in the same numbered migration.
PostgreSQL SAVEPOINT requires an explicit transaction; cross-connection DDL visibility requires autocommit creation.
